name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish inventor of Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE/ALD), pioneer in thin-film technology for electroluminescent displays and semiconductor applications.

name: Riikka L. Puurunen
summary: Author of the essay, researcher at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, historian of ALD.

name: Tampere
summary: City in Finland where Tuomo Suntola was born.

name: Turku
summary: City in Finland where Suntola completed his matriculation examinations.

name: Helsinki University of Technology
summary: Institution (now Aalto University) where Suntola studied electrical engineering and completed his doctoral thesis.

name: Thor Stubb
summary: Professor at HUT who supervised Suntola’s doctoral thesis on chalcogenide thin films.

name: VTT Semiconductor Laboratory
summary: Research laboratory in Finland where Suntola worked on humidity sensors and early ALE development.

name: Vaisala Oy
summary: Finnish company specializing in meteorological instrumentation; commissioned Suntola’s humidity sensor development.

name: Humicap 1
summary: World-leading humidity sensor developed by Suntola and Jorma Antson, patented in 1972.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish medical instrumentation company where Suntola established an ALE research group in 1974.

name: Datex Oy
summary: Subsidiary of Instrumentarium Oy focused on medical technology.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: Thin-film growth technique invented by Suntola in 1974, later renamed Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD).

name: ALE Patent (1974)
summary: International patent for ALE filed by Suntola on November 29, 1974 (Finnish priority date).

name: Jorma Antson
summary: Collaborator of Suntola in humidity sensor and early ALE development.

name: Tapio Wiik
summary: Colleague of Suntola who conducted a pre-study on humidity sensing.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Longtime collaborator of Suntola in ALE reactor design and development.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: Key collaborator in ALE development, notably involved in the ZnCl2/H2S process breakthrough.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Finnish building materials company that acquired the ALE-EL project from Instrumentarium in 1978.

name: ALE Patent (1979)
summary: Second international ALE patent for inert gas reactors and dielectric layers, filed February 28, 1979.

name: Helsinki-Vantaa Airport
summary: Site of the first public ALE-EL display installations in 1983.

name: Olarinluoma Plant
summary: EL production facility built by Lohja in Espoo, Finland, in 1984.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: American competitor that acquired Lohja’s EL business in 1990.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Company founded by Suntola in 1987 under Neste Oy to develop ALE for solar panels and catalysis.

name: Neste Oy
summary: Finnish national oil company that established Microchemistry Ltd. in 1987.

name: F-120 Reactor
summary: First commercial ALD reactor designed by Suntola and Sven Lindfors for photovoltaic research.

name: ASM Microchemistry
summary: Dutch-owned successor to Microchemistry Ltd. after its acquisition by ASM in 1999.

name: Picosun Oy
summary: ALD equipment company founded in 2004 by Sven Lindfors and Kustaa Poutiainen.

name: Beneq Oy
summary: Company that acquired Planar’s EL plant in Olarinluoma in 2012.

name: Society for Information Display
summary: Organization that hosted the 1980 SID conference where Suntola first publicly disclosed ALE-EL displays.

name: SID 1980 Conference
summary: Conference in San Diego where Suntola presented ALE-EL displays, winning the 1980 SID Outstanding Paper Award.

name: 1st International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE-1)
summary: First international ALE conference held in Espoo, Finland, in June 1990.

name: Lauri Niinistö
summary: Professor of inorganic and analytical chemistry at HUT; organized early ALE conferences and collaborated with Suntola.

name: Jun-ichi Nishizawa
summary: Japanese professor who independently explored ALE (as Molecular Layer Epitaxy) for GaAs growth.

name: Valentin B. Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet professor who co-developed the Molecular Layering (ML) technique in the 1960s.

name: Victor Drozd
summary: Russian scientist who facilitated Suntola’s 1990 visit to Leningrad to meet Aleskovskii.

name: Salah Bedair
summary: Professor at North Carolina State University who demonstrated ALE of GaAs in the 1980s.

name: Markku Leskelä
summary: Professor at the University of Helsinki, key figure in Finnish ALD research.

name: Mikko Ritala
summary: Professor at the University of Helsinki, collaborator in ALD research.

name: Elcoteq Oy
summary: Contract manufacturer spun off from Lohja’s microelectronics division in 1990.

name: Fortum Oyj
summary: Finnish energy company formed by the merger of Neste and IVO, where Suntola worked post-retirement.

name: Physics Foundations Society
summary: Organization chaired by Suntola, focused on philosophical and theoretical physics.

name: European SEMI Award 2004
summary: Award given to Suntola for pioneering ALD techniques, presented at the Munich Electronics Show 2004.

name: The Dynamic Universe
summary: Book by Suntola (2011) presenting a holistic picture of physical reality.

name: The Short History of Science
summary: Book by Suntola (2012) linking philosophy and empirical science.

name: LCD Patent (1985)
summary: Suntola’s patent on Liquid Crystal Displays (LCDs) filed in 1985, granted in 1990.

name: Tampere University of Technology
summary: Institution where Suntola lectured on semiconductor physics in the 1970s.

name: Markus Pessa
summary: Professor at TUT who led research on group III-V semiconductors using MBE.

name: Neste Advanced Power Systems
summary: Corporate venture unit of Neste Oy focused on renewable energy, including ALE-based solar panels.

name: Endeas Oy
summary: Company founded by Jaakko Hyvärinen to produce Quicksun solar simulators.

name: Picopack Oy
summary: Company founded by Ahti Aintila in 1991 for smart card production using TAB technology.

name: Ahti Aintila
summary: Engineer who developed driving circuitries and TAB technology for EL panels at Lohja.

name: Antti Piippo
summary: Business-oriented manager of Lohja’s Display Electronics division, later co-founder of Elcoteq Oy.

name: Matti Ervasti
summary: Managing director of Microchemistry Ltd. after Suntola stepped aside in 1998.

name: Pekka Soininen
summary: Founder of Beneq Oy’s ALD reactor activity in 2005.

name: Kustaa Poutiainen
summary: Co-founder of Picosun Oy in 2004.

name: Jaakko Hyvärinen
summary: Developer of the Quicksun solar simulator at Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Aimo Rautiainen
summary: Chemist at Microchemistry Ltd. who worked on ALD catalysts.

name: Eeva-Liisa Lakomaa
summary: Chemist at Microchemistry Ltd. involved in ALD catalyst research.

name: Marina Lindblad
summary: Researcher at Microchemistry Ltd. who completed a doctoral thesis on ZnS growth in 1992.

name: Suvi Haukka
summary: Researcher who completed a doctoral thesis on ALD in 1993.

name: Arla Kytökivi
summary: Researcher who completed a doctoral thesis on ALD in 1997.

name: Tapani Pakkanen
summary: Professor at the University of Joensuu who collaborated on quantum chemical analysis of ZnS growth.

name: Heli Vaara
summary: Assistant to Tuomo Suntola at Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Ulf Ström
summary: Managing director of Finlux Inc., responsible for marketing ALE-EL panels in the USA.

name: Finlux Inc.
summary: Company involved in marketing ALE-EL panels in the USA.

name: Ralf Graeffe
summary: Researcher who inspected display modules in Helsinki-Vantaa Airport’s underground test assembly.

name: Tapio Alvesalo
summary: Head of Neste’s venture team (NAPS) who initiated ALE-based solar panel research.

name: Yukihiro Shimogaki
summary: Professor who helped identify participants in the ALE-1 photograph.

name: David Cameron
summary: Professor who polished the language of Puurunen’s essay.

name: Academy of Finland’s Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Funding body for ALD research in Finland, acknowledged in Puurunen’s essay.

name: Virtual Project on the History of ALD
summary: Worldwide open voluntary effort to document the history of ALD, mentioned in the essay.

name: 40 Years of ALD in Finland – Photos, Stories
summary: Exhibition organized in 2014 to celebrate the 40th anniversary of ALD in Finland.

name: MRS 1994 Annual Meeting
summary: Conference in Boston where Suntola introduced ALE for semiconductor applications.

name: F-450 Reactor
summary: ALD reactor designed by Microchemistry Ltd. for processing silicon wafers and large glass substrates.

name: F-1000 Reactor
summary: Large ALD reactor by Microchemistry Ltd. for coating 500 mm × 500 mm substrate batches.

name: Quicksun Simulator
summary: Solar simulator developed by Jaakko Hyvärinen for testing PV panels.

name: INSKO
summary: Finnish organization where Suntola gave lectures on display technologies.

name: San Diego
summary: Location of the SID 1980 conference and ICVGE-5 (1981).

name: Kobe
summary: Location of the 16th International Conference on Solid State Devices and Materials (1984).

name: Leningrad
summary: Soviet city (now St. Petersburg) where Suntola met Aleskovskii in 1990.

name: Boston
summary: Location of the MRS 1994 Annual Meeting.

name: Munich
summary: Location of the Munich Electronics Show 2004 where Suntola received the SEMI Award.

name: Espoo
summary: Finnish city where Suntola worked and where key ALE conferences were held.

name: Joensuu
summary: Finnish city home to the University of Joensuu, where Tapani Pakkanen collaborated on ALE research.

name: North Carolina State University
summary: Institution where Professor Bedair demonstrated ALE of GaAs in the 1980s.

name: University of Southern California
summary: Institution where Professor DenBaars demonstrated ALD of GaAs in MO-CVD systems.

name: Nippon Electric Company
summary: Japanese company (NEC) that demonstrated ALE-grown InGaP-GaAs-InGaP superlattices.

name: CGE
summary: French state-owned company that licensed ALE-EL technology from Lohja in 1983.

name: Sintra Alcatel
summary: French company that inherited the ALE-EL license from CGE.

name: RIKEN
summary: Japanese research institute where Yoshinobu Aoyagi worked.

name: Yoshinobu Aoyagi
summary: Researcher at RIKEN who attended the ALE-1 conference.
